newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress opposes oil price increase - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress opposes oil price increase - PTI.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Friday that it opposed any increase in the prices of petroleum products to control a soaring subsidy bill, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

"We are strongly opposed to any increase and we hope the government will come out with an alternative proposal to deal with the issue," the news agency quoted Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil as saying.
Gadgil was speaking to reporters following a meeting on Thursday between Congress president Sitaram Kesri and Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral.
Gujral's ruling United Front coalition is set to meet on July 2 to consider raising the prices of some petroleum products.

At its last meeting on June 16, the alliance deferred a decision on whether to raise prices to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.
This week the alliance, deeply divided over the issue, postponed a meeting set for Friday until July 2.
Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram favour raising the prices of some petroleum prices, but they are strongly opposed by left-wing parties in the coalition.

Information Minister Jaipal Reddy, who is also the United Front spokesman, said on Thursday that the 15-party centre-left coalition would take a final decision on the oil price question at next Wednesday's meeting.
Congress was waiting for the United Front to propose an alternative to price increases, PTI quoted Gadgil as saying.
The communist parties in Gujral's coalition have proposed lowering import duties on some petroleum products and writing off the debt to the state-owned oil firms as an alternative.
